title: Batching & Cache Advisor cards + Rollback Playbook
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Purpose: Design a compact, explainable advisor UI surface in the Redwood Console that recommends batching and prefix/KV cache presets, shows estimated latency/cost impact, and provides an operator playbook for safe rollbacks. This ticket covers: advisor card UI patterns, inline explainers for each recommended change, a one-click 'apply preset' flow with simulated impact preview, and an ops rollback playbook accessible from the same surface.

User problems: Engineers and platform owners struggle to tune batching/cache without risking increased latency or degradations. Current flows surface raw knobs but lack clear recommendations, cost trade-offs, or easy recovery steps when changes cause regressions.

Goals:
- Surface 2–4 ranked recommendations per route/model with concise rationale and confidence score.
- Provide an interactive simulation panel that estimates per-token cost, p95 latency, and expected throughput change for the selected preset.
- Offer guardrail indicators (safety thresholds) and require explicit acknowledgement for risky recommendations (e.g., >20% estimated latency regression).
- Enable a single-click apply with an optional canary rollout (5–10% traffic) and tie to automatic telemetry so regressions trigger rollback.
- Document an operator rollback playbook that is discoverable from the UI and includes step-by-step mitigation actions.

Constraints & assumptions:
- We must use runtime-provided metrics (p50/p95 latency, token counts) for simulation; simulations are estimates, not guarantees.
- All recommendations must be reversible via console or API.
- Security: no exposure of customer prompt payloads — simulations must use synthetic or sanitized examples.

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity Figma prototypes for desktop and tablet approved by PM and Eng.
- Usability test with 5 internal engineers showing task success >=80% for applying a preset and reverting it.
- Telemetry events defined for: recommendation_shown, preset_simulated, preset_applied, canary_started, canary_failed, rollback_initiated.
- Frontend PR (linked in comments) implements the UI screens and toggles; backend contract for canary + telemetry implemented by ENG.
- Rollback playbook content reviewed and published in the Console help center.

Metrics of success:
- Reduction in manual tuning incidents (tracked via support tickets) for batching/cache related customer issues by 30% within 8 weeks.
- At least 40% of recommended presets applied by new users within their first three sessions.

Accessibility notes: use clear text labels for confidence and impact, color-blind friendly palettes for guardrail states, keyboard-accessible controls for apply/revert actions.

Privacy & compliance: mark simulation inputs as synthetic; do not persist customer inputs in preview mode.

Rollout plan: staged behind feature flag; 10% of org can opt-in for early feedback; full rollout after 2 weeks and successful canary metrics.

2025-02-20 - Ethan Park (PM): Reviewed goals. PM asks that the advisor highlight cost-first vs latency-first presets and include a toggle to prioritize either objective. Also requested telemetry names to match analytics schema; see attachments.

2025-02-25 - Design critique (team): Feedback: simplify confidence label language (Suggested: 'High / Medium / Low' vs raw percentage). Add an 'explain why' flyout that surfaces the top 2 factors contributing to the recommendation (e.g., short-sequence bias, high KV hit rate).

2025-02-27 - Prototype testing session: Conducted 6 internal sessions with infra and platform engineers. Observations: users like the simulation preview but want clearer failure modes and faster access to rollback steps. Updated prototype to move rollback actions into a persistent header when in 'canary' state.

2025-03-03 - Accessibility review: Keyboard flows verified for applying and dismissing the simulation panel. Need additional aria-labels for the confidence badges. Assigned small follow-up to update labels prior to merge.
